articles.title: FuriosaAI Series D: $620m quadruples the chipmaker's value to $2.9bn

facts.fact: FuriosaAI, a Seoul-based maker of AI inference chips, raised $620m in a Series D round at a valuation of about $2.9bn.

The money goes to more RNGD chips, software and a third-generation chip, developed with Broadcom and other partners, a 2nm multi-die design with HBM4 memory.

articles.title: 카카오, 개인화 AI 에이전트용 임베딩 모델 2종 오픈소스 공개
articles.title_en: Kakao releases two embedding models for personalised AI agents as open source

facts.fact: Kakao released two 'Kanana-2-embedding' models on Hugging Face as open source: Kanana-2-3b-embedding (3 billion parameters) and Kanana-2-1.3b-embedding (1.3 billion).
An embedding model turns the meaning of text into numbers so an AI can find information related to a question by semantic similarity, even when the user does not remember the exact words.
Example in the article: a user asking for 'the quiet restaurant we talked about before' can find a past message about 'a good place to talk' without typing the restaurant name.

By Kakao's own evaluation the models beat similar-size open models llama-nemotron-embed-1b-v2 and Qwen3-Embedding-4B on Korean, with similar English performance, and were more efficient at inference than Qwen3-Embedding.
The 1.3B model was built by distilling the 3B model. A technique called Matryoshka Representation Learning lets developers choose the vector size to trade search quality against storage and speed.
Both models use the 'Kanana Open License', which allows commercial use. It follows four small Kanana language models released in July.

articles.title: DeepSeek, Moonshot used OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra to train latest models, The Information reports

facts.fact: Chinese AI developers DeepSeek and Moonshot AI relied heavily on outputs from OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra to train their latest models, The Information reported, citing people with direct knowledge.
The practice is called distillation. Firms argue it lets rivals reproduce advanced capabilities more quickly and cheaply.
Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro, released last week, and DeepSeek's upgraded V4.1-Flash 1017, launched Oct 17, benefited from distilling Astra, according to The Information.
OpenAI, DeepSeek and Moonshot did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.
In a Sept 30 blog post OpenAI said it had linked a core part of a distillation campaign that began in July to individuals associated with Moonshot.
Earlier this month Anthropic said new measures cut data harvested in distillation attacks by about 90% to 99%.

candidates.notes: Short wire text, single source, claim is unconfirmed (anonymous sources). Count as Asia only if the editor treats China as Asia.
